title: etbb-july-2024-february-2026-update.pdf — section 350
text:
133. On 27 February 2023, the Marriage and Civil Partnership (Minimum Age) Act 2022 raised
the minimum age of marriage in England and Wales to 18. Although 16 and 17 year olds had
required parental consent to be married, this was stated to be an attempt to end coercive or
abusive child marriages, which disproportionately affect a greater number of girls, usually
married to older men. In England and Wales in 2018, 28 boys married under the age of 18,
compared with 119 girls. In 2021, the FMU provided advice or support in 118 cases involving
victims below 18 years of age. The courts have also issued 3,343 Forced Marriage
Protection Orders between their introduction in 2008 and September 2022, which prevents
someone from using threats, violence or emotional abuse as a way to force a person into
marriage.
